Change c0431. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. V; 1831 Ch. XXII.

Context before (unchanged): But this is false reasoning.

1818 text: I confess to you, my cousin, that I love you, and that in my airy dreams of futurity you have been my constant friend and companion.

1831 text: I confess to you, my friend, that I love you, and that in my airy dreams of futurity you have been my constant friend and companion.

Diff: I confess to you, my [-cousin-] {+friend+} , that I love you, and that in my airy dreams of futurity you have been my constant friend and companion.

Context after (unchanged): But it is your happiness I desire as well as my own, when I declare to you, that our marriage would render me eternally miserable, unless it were the dictate of your own free choice.

result.rationale: Replacing "my cousin" with "my friend" removes the kinship between Elizabeth and Victor, changing how their relationship is defined in a passage about marriage and free choice; the blood tie is erased, so the marriage reads differently.
